spatial_claims.claim: ABC is an equilateral triangle inscribed in circle ABC; A, B, C lie on the circumference
D is the center of the circle; DA = DB = DE are all radii
AE is a diameter passing through center D, with D between A and E
Angle ADB (central) and angle ACB (inscribed) stand on the same arc AB; angle ADB = 2 times angle ACB
DB stands on line AE at D, so angles ADB and BDE are supplementary (sum to 180 degrees)
In triangle DBE, DB = DE (radii), so base angles DBE and DEB are equal
Triangle DBE is equilateral; BE = DE = radius
B lies on semicircle with diameter AE, so angle ABE = 90 degrees (III.31)
Triangle ABE is right-angled at B; AE squared = AB squared + BE squared
AE = AD + DE with AD = DE, so AE squared = 4 times DE squared
AB squared = 4 DE squared minus DE squared = 3 DE squared

configuration_map: Circle with center D and radius r. Equilateral triangle ABC inscribed with vertices on circumference, each arc (AB, BC, CA) spanning 120 degrees, each interior angle 60 degrees. E is the second intersection of line AD with the circle (antipodal to A), making AE a diameter of length 2r. D lies between A and E with AD = DE = r. Central angle ADB = 120 degrees (subtending 120-degree arc AB). Supplementary angle BDE = 60 degrees. Triangle DBE has DB = DE = r and angle BDE = 60 degrees, making it equilateral with BE = r. Triangle ABE has right angle at B (angle in semicircle), hypotenuse AE = 2r, legs AB (side of equilateral triangle) and BE = r.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof establishes BE = DE through a valid chain of angle calculations (III.20 for the central angle, I.13 for supplementary angles on the diameter, then I.5 and I.6 in the isosceles triangle DBE). No angle decomposition requires a hidden betweenness assumption; the only supplementary relationship (ADB + BDE = 180 degrees) is justified by D lying between A and E on the diameter. The right angle at B from III.31 is correctly applied since B is on the semicircle with diameter AE. The final algebraic steps follow directly from the established equalities.
